title: Nirenberg and Matthaei linked RNA composition to protein synthesis
summary: Their 1961 PNAS paper is an early decoding experiment, not the finished codon table.
body: Marshall W. Nirenberg and J. Heinrich Matthaei, "The dependence of cell-free protein synthesis in E. coli upon naturally occurring or synthetic polyribonucleotides" (Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 1961), showed that synthetic RNA could direct amino-acid incorporation in a cell-free system. It is a founding decoding experiment. The full table of 64 codons was assembled across later papers. The v1 article's "three bases = one codon" and "64 codons, 20 amino acids" are stated as a finished code on the OpenStax and genome.gov cards, not as the whole content of this 1961 paper.
